title: Nonzero homogeneous relations lower cumulative polynomial-ring Hilbert growth
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $d\geq1$ be an integer, and let $P=k[T_1,\ldots,T_d]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], with total-degree homogeneous subspaces $P_j$ spanned by the monomials of degree $j$. Let $I\subset P$ be a nonzero proper homogeneous ideal: if $f\in I$, every total-degree homogeneous component of $f$ also belongs to $I$. Put $M=P/I$ and $M_j=\operatorname{im}(P_j\to M)$, so $M=\bigoplus_{j\geq0}M_j$. Each $M_j$ is finite-dimensional over $k$ [def-weil-vector-space-dimension]. For integers $n\geq1$ put $h_I(n)=\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}\dim_k M_j$. There exist a nonzero polynomial $Q_I\in\mathbf Q[X]$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring] with strictly positive leading coefficient and an integer $N\geq1$ such that $h_I(n)=Q_I(n)$ for all integers $n\geq N$ and $\deg Q_I<d$.

source.place: Tag 00K3 (lemma-quotient-smaller-d), read with Tag 00JZ (lemma-numerical-polynomial): sum the eventual degree-piece Hilbert polynomial. If the degree-piece polynomial is zero the cumulative polynomial is a positive constant, including d=1.

proof.text: Use the total-degree grading of $P$. Homogeneity of $I$ implies $I=\bigoplus_{j\geq0}(I\cap P_j)$: taking components preserves membership, and uniqueness follows from uniqueness of monomial coefficients. Consequently $M_j\simeq P_j/(I\cap P_j)$, and $M$ is a cyclic graded $P$-module generated by $1$. Each $P_j$ has the finite basis of degree-$j$ monomials, whose images span $M_j$. Since a nonzero constant in $I$ would be invertible, properness gives $I\cap k=0$ and $M_0=k$. Thus $h_I(n)\geq1$ for every $n\geq1$.

source.place: Tag 00K3, lemma-quotient-smaller-d, proof; cumulative-degree version of the monomial dimension bound

proof.text: The algebra $P$ is standard graded: $P_0=k$, multiplication adds degrees, and the finite family $T_1,\ldots,T_d$ in degree one generates it. Apply [lem-trf-standard-graded-hilbert-function] to $S=P$ and the cyclic graded module $M=P/I$. It supplies $A\in\mathbf Q[X]$ and an integer $n_0\geq1$ (enlarge its threshold if necessary) such that $\dim_k M_j=A(j)$ for every $j\geq n_0$. The polynomial $A$ may be zero.

For $t\in\mathbf N$ set $F(t)=h_I(n_0+t)$. The defining finite sums give $F(t+1)-F(t)=\dim_k M_{n_0+t}=A(n_0+t)$. Put $\widetilde A(X)=A(X+n_0)$ and choose $b=0$ if $A=0$, otherwise $b=\deg A+1$; translation does not increase degree, by expanding each power of $X+n_0$, so $\deg\widetilde A<b$. Apply [lem-trf-rational-sequence-polynomial-forward-difference] to $F$, viewed as rational-valued, and $\widetilde A$. Obtain $R\in\mathbf Q[X]$ with $R(t)=F(t)$ for all natural $t$. Then $Q_I(X)=R(X-n_0)$ satisfies $Q_I(n)=h_I(n)$ for every integer $n\geq n_0$.

source.place: Tag 00JZ, lemma-numerical-polynomial, applied to the cumulative Hilbert function after translating the threshold

proof.text: Choose $0\ne g\in I$. At least one of its finitely many homogeneous components is nonzero; choose such a component $f\in I\cap P_e$. It has degree $e\geq1$: a nonzero degree-zero component would be a nonzero constant in the proper ideal $I$, contradicting step 1.

source.place: Tag 00K3, lemma-quotient-smaller-d, proof; cumulative-degree version of the monomial dimension bound

proof.text: For $n\geq1$ let $V_n=\bigoplus_{0\leq j<n}P_j$. Its monomial basis is indexed by tuples $(a_1,\ldots,a_d)\in\mathbf N^d$ with $\sum a_i<n$. Adjoin the slack entry $a_0=n-1-\sum a_i$. This is a bijection with $(d+1)$-tuples summing to $n-1$. Encoding such a tuple by $n-1$ stars and $d$ separators, with $a_i$ stars in the $i$th gap, bijects it with the $d$-element subsets of $n+d-1$ positions. Hence $\dim_k V_n=\binom{n+d-1}{d}=B(n)$, where $B(X)=X(X+1)\cdots(X+d-1)/d!\in\mathbf Q[X]$. This is a direct finite basis count, valid also for $n=1$ and $d=1$.

source.place: Tag 00K3, lemma-quotient-smaller-d, proof; cumulative-degree version of the monomial dimension bound

proof.text: Fix $n\geq e+1$. By [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-domain], $P$ is a domain. Multiplication by $f\ne0$ is therefore injective on $V_{n-e}$ and its image is contained in $K_n=I\cap V_n$, since $f$ has degree $e$ and $I$ is an ideal. The image of a basis of $V_{n-e}$ is linearly independent in $K_n$, so $\dim_k K_n\geq\dim_k V_{n-e}$. The quotient map identifies $V_n/K_n$ with $\bigoplus_{j<n}M_j$ by step 1. The quotient dimension identity [lem-trf-vector-space-quotient-dimension] gives $h_I(n)=\dim_k V_n-\dim_k K_n\leq B(n)-B(n-e)$.

source.place: Tag 00K3, lemma-quotient-smaller-d, proof; cumulative-degree version of the monomial dimension bound

proof.text: Put $D(X)=B(X)-B(X-e)$. The product defining $B$ has degree $d$ and leading coefficient $1/d!$. In the expansion of $B(X-e)$, the coefficient of $X^d$ is again $1/d!$, and that of $X^{d-1}$ is the coefficient in $B$ minus $de/d!$. Thus $D$ has degree exactly $d-1$ and positive leading coefficient $e/(d-1)!$. This includes $d=1$, where $B(X)=X$ and $D(X)=e$. Combining steps 1, 3 and 6 gives $1\leq Q_I(n)\leq D(n)$ for every integer $n\geq\max(n_0,e+1)$.

source.place: Tag 00K3, lemma-quotient-smaller-d, proof; cumulative-degree version of the monomial dimension bound

proof.text: The lower bound shows $Q_I\ne0$. Write $r=\deg Q_I$ and $a$ for its nonzero leading coefficient. Apply [lem-sfb-polynomial-leading-term-asymptotic] with $\epsilon=1/2$. If $a<0$, then for sufficiently large positive integers $n$ it yields $Q_I(n)\leq a n^r/2<0$, a contradiction. Hence $a>0$, and the same estimate gives $Q_I(n)\geq a n^r/2$. Apply the cited asymptotic statement also to $D$, whose leading coefficient is $c=e/(d-1)!>0$; eventually $D(n)\leq3c n^{d-1}/2$. If $r\geq d$, the two bounds imply $a n^{r-d+1}\leq3c$ for all sufficiently large integers $n$, contradicted by $n>\max(1,3c/a)$. Therefore $\deg Q_I=r<d$. Take $N=n_0\geq1$ for eventual equality; positivity and the degree bound are properties of this same $Q_I$.
